name: equal-weight-subsignals-current-config
rationale: Literature-motivated. Wen, Bouri, Xu & Zhao (2022) find Bitcoin intraday returns show BOTH momentum and reversal, with the dominant pattern shifting by regime (around jumps, FOMC, liquidity). That argues against hard-coding either family as dominant. dev ships reversion 1.0 / trend 0.25 (chosen on hourly CoinGecko data), while on 2026-10-19 two independent trend-heavier variants (trend-weight-half, trend-weighted-subsignals) improved results at every diagnostic capital. Equal weights (1.0 / 1.0) is the neutral point the paper's 'both' finding suggests, and it brackets trend-weight-half (0.5) from the other side, so the two together walk the weight curve on the current baseline config.
code_change_summary: In TradingEngine::compute_btc_target (src/trading/engine.rs), change the single constant TREND_SUBSIGNAL_WEIGHT from 0.25 to 1.0, leaving REVERSION_SUBSIGNAL_WEIGHT at 1.0, so all five sub-signals are weighted equally. Nothing else changes: every sub-signal formula (RSI, damped SMA cross, damped EMA cross, damped MACD histogram / step fallback, Bollinger %B), the weighted-mean aggregation, the empty-sub_signals warmup guard, the non-positive SMA/EMA guards and the sentiment combination stay byte-for-byte identical. Update the constant's doc comment (and the doc comment on compute_btc_target that lists the weights) to record that 1.0 is an equal-weight probe motivated by Wen et al. (2022). Then update the expected values in the compute_btc_target_* unit tests wherever the new weight legitimately changes them; in particular compute_btc_target_mean_reverting_family_dominates_trend_disagreement asserts reversion dominance, which equal weighting removes by design -- rewrite that test to assert the new equal-weight arithmetic rather than deleting it.
constraints: This hypothesis modifies the body of TradingEngine::compute_btc_target. This change MUST be made only on this hypothesis's own dedicated isolation: "worktree" branch -- never as a direct commit to dev/main.
MUST NOT change TradingEngine::compute_btc_target's signature (its parameter list or return type) -- only its body.
MUST NOT change any individual sub-signal's own formula, the aggregation expression, or REVERSION_SUBSIGNAL_WEIGHT; exactly one numeric constant changes.

MUST pass `cargo test`, including the compute_btc_target_* unit tests in src/trading/engine.rs -- update their expected values if the new weight legitimately changes them (do not weaken or delete a test just to make it pass).

A promoted change still becomes its own PR against dev (per the pipeline's step 6) and is never merged automatically -- a human reviews it like any other algorithm hypothesis. Flag explicitly in the PR description that this diff touches compute_btc_target's body, so the reviewer gives it the scrutiny an allocation-formula change deserves.
MUST NOT touch src/exchange/bitflyer/*, .github/workflows/*, or anything on the live order-submission path.

paper_reference.title: Intraday return predictability in the cryptocurrency markets: Momentum, reversal, or both
paper_reference.authors: Zhuzhu Wen, Elie Bouri, Yahua Xu, Yang Zhao
paper_reference.venue_year: North American Journal of Economics and Finance 62, 2022
paper_reference.key_claim: High-frequency Bitcoin returns (2013-2020) show both intraday momentum and reversal, with the dominant pattern switching around jumps, FOMC days, liquidity and COVID; timing strategies on these predictors beat buy-and-hold.
paper_reference.pros: Same asset, intraday horizon, and directly addresses the momentum-vs-reversion weighting question that the 2026-10-19 run's results raised.
paper_reference.cons: Predictors are half-hour session returns, not 1-minute TA sub-signals; sample ends 2020 and predates the current liquidity regime; spot-index data rather than bitFlyer BTC/JPY; fee/slippage treatment unknown from the abstract (full text paywalled). The paper says the dominant pattern is regime-dependent, which a fixed equal weight does not capture.
